Subject: Re: Finora DPA redlines + BYO-key ask

Caroline — thanks for sending this over and for the clarity on BYOK. Looping in Priya (security lead) and Marcus (commercial/procurement) to draft a consolidated response.

Initial positions from our side:
- Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) via customer KMS. We do not persist plaintext customer keys. For cloud KMS customers can provide a key-wrapping key (KMS ARN) that we use to encrypt at rest.
- For HSM-grade requirements we can support CMEK backed by provider HSMs (e.g., AWS KMS with HSM) or customer-managed HSMs when deployed on Private.
- We generally avoid full key escrow because it undermines BYOK guarantees, but we recognize procurement asks. We can offer a limited-minded escrow mechanism that requires dual approvals and legal attestation plus an auditable process (see attached TOMs draft).

Next steps: Priya — can you prepare a TOMs exhibit that includes the BYOK handshake, a brief escrow SOP (if we offer it as an opt-in), and the audit/logging commitments? Marcus — can you propose two procurement language options (one with no escrow, one with gated escrow) so Finora can choose? I will coordinate execution (DocuSign) after we have agreed text.

Hannah
VP, Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>

Subject: TOMs exhibit v0.2 for Finora (BYOK + escrow outline)

Team — attached is a first pass TOMs exhibit that tries to balance Finora's security posture and our operational model. Key excerpts included in the doc:
- Encryption-at-rest: AES-256-GCM for persisted data; customer-provided wrapping via Cloud KMS (CMEK) supported.
- Key custody: Redwood will not persist plaintext customer keys. KMS ARNs or wrapped keys are stored encrypted via server-side platform keys.
- BYOK handshake: onboarding step where customer provides a KMS binding (ARN/URI) and we perform a short verification (test encrypt/decrypt).
- Emergency access / escrow: optional escrow repository managed by a certified third-party custodian. Escrow release requires (a) joint attestation by customer + Redwood, or (b) court order + notarized request, and (c) access logged and time-limited.
- Access controls & audits: role-based access with separation of duties, quarterly key rotation policy, full audit trail retained 1 year by default (extendable).

Notes / trade-offs: the escrow option adds procurement friction and custodian fees; operationally we can keep escrow as an opt-in paid add-on. The doc includes proposed contract language for Section 4.3 (Key Management) and Exhibit B.

Attachment: TOMs-exhibit_BYO-KMS_v2.docx

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Director, InfoSec | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: TOMs exhibit v0.2 for Finora (BYOK + escrow outline)

Appreciate the thoughtful draft. From a commercial/procurement perspective, Finora is likely to push for an escrow path unless presented with a clean alternative. To speed sign-off, I recommend we surface two concise options in the DPA:

Option A (Standard BYOK):
- Customer supplies KMS binding; Redwood never accesses plaintext keys; no escrow; Redwood provides operational runbook and verification steps.

Option B (BYOK + Escrow):
- Same as A, plus optional escrow maintained by a neutral custodian. Escrow release requires dual attestations and documented emergency conditions; escrow adds a fixed monthly/admin fee.

I can put these into the DPA redline as clear alternatives (so procurement can pick). Also suggest we prepare the DocuSign envelope with pre-filled Exhibit B and the two-option toggle to avoid back-and-forth. If Hannah approves, I'll prepare the DocuSign draft and route it through legal for final review.

Marcus
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Finora DPA redlines + BYO-key ask — consolidated response & next steps

Caroline / Tom — thank you for the redlines and context. Attached is our consolidated response and an updated DPA that surfaces two clear options for Exhibit B (see Section 4.3): Option A (Standard BYOK — no escrow) and Option B (BYOK + Escrow custodian with release controls). Highlights:
- We will not retain plaintext customer keys and will support customer-supplied KMS ARNs for key wrapping (CMEK).
- HSM-grade support is available via provider HSMs or Private deployment where relevant.
- Escrow is optional and treated as a gated service with clear release criteria, dual attestation, and audit logging.

Please review Option A vs Option B and let us know which you prefer by EOD Friday. If either option works, we will prepare the DocuSign envelope (I can arrange for execution the following week) — linking the HubSpot deal (RDW-4592) so procurement can liaise on billing.
